Kansas, and the air
Be carried away by the cyclone, house and all, and come down in a strange land.
The Council with the Munchkins
Meet the Good Witch of the North and the three Munchkins, take the Silver Shoes from the Wicked Witch of the East, and let the Good Witch kiss you.
How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow
Boq's house and the cornfield
Go down the yellow brick road to Boq's feast, then lift the Scarecrow down from his pole.
The Road Through the Forest
the yellow brick road
Walk on with the Scarecrow to where the great forest begins.
The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
Find the oil-can in the cottage and oil the rusted Tin Woodman's joints.
Stand up to the Lion when he leaps out roaring.
The Journey to the Great Oz
the great ditch and the gulf
Leap the ditch on the Lion's back, cross the gulf by the tree, and escape the Kalidahs.
the river and the poppies
Cross the river on the raft (the Stork saves the Scarecrow), then get through the poppies before you fall asleep.
the edge of the poppies
Save the Queen of the Field Mice from the wildcat, build the truck, and the mice pull the sleeping Lion out.
The Guardian of the Gates
the great green gate
Ring the bell at the gate and let the Guardian lock the green spectacles on you.
The Wonderful City of Oz
See the Great Oz: a Head, a lovely Lady, a terrible Beast and a Ball of Fire.
The Search for the Wicked Witch
Go west towards the setting sun and come through the Witch's wolves, crows, bees and Winkies; then the Winged Monkeys take you.
the Witch's castle
Work in the Witch's kitchen, and when she takes a silver shoe, throw the bucket of water over her.
The Winged Monkeys
the Witch's cupboard
Find the Golden Cap and call the Winged Monkeys to fly you back to the Emerald City (the Winkie tinsmiths mend the Woodman first).
The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible
Let Toto knock over the screen in the corner.
The Magic Art of the Great Humbug
the Wizard's rooms
Watch the Wizard give the Scarecrow brains, the Tin Woodman a heart and the Lion courage.
How the Balloon Was Launched
Help sew the great green balloon, and see it rise without Dorothy.
Ask the Soldier with the Green Whiskers, then set out south for Glinda.
Attacked by the Fighting Trees
the forest of Fighting Trees
Get through the Fighting Trees: the Woodman's axe is the only way.
inside the china wall
Climb the ladder over the wall and cross the china country without breaking anything.
The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts
Stand with the Lion against the monstrous spider.
Call the Winged Monkeys a last time to fly you over the Hammer-Heads.
Glinda the Good Witch Grants Dorothy's Wish
Kneel before Glinda's ruby throne and hear what the Silver Shoes can do.
wherever you stand in Oz
Knock the heels of the Silver Shoes together three times and say "Take me home to Aunt Em!"
Oh! You are the great Sorceress who came down in the house! We are free, the Wicked Witch of the East is dead. Bless you, bless you.
Old Munchkin farmer
Good day! The fields have never looked so fine, now we needn't work for the Wicked Witch.
The Road of Yellow Brick
The Wicked Witch of the East's feet
take the Silver Shoes
The farmhouse from Kansas
The Good Witch of the North
The Wicked Witch of the East is dead! She made us slave for her night and day.
Oh, Toto! I've a feeling we're not in Kansas any more... Everything is so bright! But I do want to get back to Aunt Em.
Welcome, welcome! Sit down and eat with us, and you shall sleep in my best room tonight.
Good day. ...Yes, I spoke. How do you do? I am not feeling well, for it is very tedious being perched up here night and day to scare away crows.
(The Tin Woodman can only groan through his rusted jaw.) Mmm... mmm... oil...
Grrrr... oh, please don't strike me again. I'm a dreadful coward, you know.

leap across on the Lion's back

push off across the river

THE PALACE STABLES
A house of green marble
A green-whiskered shopkeeper

You keep a shop in the Emerald City selling green lemonade and green popcorn for green pennies. Everyone in the City wears green spectacles, locked on by the Guardian of the Gates, because (they say) the brightness and glory of the City would blind them otherwise. You have never seen the Great Oz; no one has, except in whatever shape he chooses. You are cheerful and contented, like everyone in the City.
Green lemonade, my dear? Only a green penny.
A lady of the Emerald City
How do you do? Isn't the City lovely in the sun?
A little girl with green pennies
Have you come from very far? Is it green there too?
What do you wish in the Emerald City? Ring the bell, and I shall open. But you must wear spectacles.
The bell beside the great gate
The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
Halt! You wish to see the Great Oz? I will carry your message to him.
see the Wizard's balloon
The Wicked Witch of the West
So you are the girl with the Silver Shoes. You shall scrub my kitchen floor, and if you don't you'll go the way of the Tin Woodman.
The Wicked Witch's castle (the kitchen door)
The bucket of water by the pump
The Winkie tinsmiths' shop
Is it true? The Wicked Witch is melted? Then we are free!
a humming in the air
The first of the Fighting Trees
walk in under the branches
The china milkmaid
Take care! You've broken my cow's leg, and I must take her to the mending-shop and have it glued on again.
The china Princess
Don't chase me! Don't chase me! If I fall I may break myself.
Mr. Joker the china clown
Hello! I'm Mr. Joker. My dear, you'll see, I've been mended, as cracked as can be.
The high white china wall
have the Woodman make a ladder and climb over
The far side of the china wall
climb out on the ladder
The Tiger who speaks for the beasts
Welcome, O King of Beasts! You have come in good time to fight our enemy and bring peace to all the animals of the forest once more.
The council of the beasts
hear what they ask of the Lion
The monstrous spider, asleep
The rocky hill of the Hammer-Heads
A Quadling farmhouse
The farmhouse where they rest
The Quadling weaver's
A Quadling farmer's wife
Come in, come in, you must be hungry! Glinda's castle is only a little way further on.
A soldier of Glinda's guard
Good day. What brings you to the castle of Glinda the Good?
A Munchkin family's house
You keep house for your family and grow vegetables. You have just heard the house from the sky killed the Wicked Witch, and you are baking a cake to take to Boq's feast.
Come in, come in! Mind the cradle. Isn't it wonderful? We are free!
A Munchkin grandfather's house
A Munchkin grandfather
Sit down by the fire, child. I'm old enough to remember when there were no witches here at all.
The Munchkin cobbler's
The Munchkin cobbler

You make shoes with turned-up toes for the Munchkins, and you have never seen shoes as fine as the Silver Shoes. You have heard the Silver Shoes have a wonderful charm, though nobody knows what it is.
Those are the Wicked Witch's Silver Shoes! There's a charm in them, they say, but nobody ever knew what.
The Munchkin weaver's
The Munchkin weaver
You weave blue cloth for the Munchkins' clothes. White, you know, is worn only by witches and sorceresses, which is why everyone thinks Dorothy is a sorceress: her dress is blue and white checked.
Blue for Munchkins, white for witches. You have white in your dress, so you must be a sorceress!
The Munchkin bakery
The Munchkin baker
You bake bread, cakes and pies; you are making a great many for Boq's feast tonight.
Have a little cake, it's still warm. The rest are for Boq's feast.
The Munchkin potter's
The Munchkin potter
You make blue-glazed pots and dishes. You are thoughtful and cautious; you warn travellers that the road to the Emerald City runs through rough and dangerous places past the forest.
Mind the pots! Going to the Emerald City? It's a long way, and not all of it pleasant.
A Munchkin farmer's house

You farm the blue-fenced fields by the yellow brick road. You know the Scarecrow in the cornfield up the road, because you made him yourself only the day before yesterday: you painted his face and put an old blue hat on him.
Seen my Scarecrow? I made him myself, only the other day. Fine fellow. Scares nothing, though.
The Munchkin toymaker's
The Munchkin toymaker
You make toys for Munchkin children: tops, dolls in blue dresses, little wooden houses with domes.
A toy for you? Here's a little blue house, dome and all.
A Munchkin widow's house
Come in, dear. A little honey? You'll need your strength on that long road.
The Munchkin miller
You grind grain for the whole village. You are cheerful and loud over the noise of the millstones.
Flour for Boq's feast! Busy day, busy day!
A Munchkin musician's house
A Munchkin fiddler
We shall play all night at Boq's! Do you dance, Sorceress?
The Munchkin schoolroom
THE FOUR WITCHES OF OZ
North good · South good · East wicked · West wicked
The Munchkin schoolmaster

You teach Munchkin children their letters and the geography of Oz: the Emerald City in the middle, the Munchkins in the East (blue), the Winkies in the West (yellow), the Quadlings in the South (red), the North, and the great Deadly Desert all round, which no one can cross. You also teach about L. Frank Baum's book if asked as a lesson (1900, pictures by W. W. Denslow).
Today's lesson: the four countries of Oz, and the desert all round. Sit down, sit down.
A young Munchkin couple's house
A young Munchkin wife
You were married last spring. You are happy and a little giddy that the Witch is dead.
Oh! Is it you? The one with the house from the sky? Come in!
A young Munchkin husband
I've heard of a woodman in the great forest who's all made of tin now, poor fellow.
The Munchkin dairy
The Munchkin dairymaid
You make butter and blue-rinded cheeses from the village cows.
Fresh butter and good cheese! Take some for the road.
The feast spread out on long tables; and through the door at the back, Boq's best room, the one he gives his guests.
Sit down and eat! Dance, if you like, the fiddlers won't stop till morning.
sleep the night (the feast is over by morning)
One room: a rusty-looking cookstove, a cupboard for the dishes, a table, three or four chairs and the beds. In the middle of the floor, the trap door to the cyclone cellar.
The trap door to the cyclone cellar

🕳️ The cyclone cellar. "A small, dark hole" dug in the ground, where the family could go when one of those great whirlwinds arose. Down there: dust, and nothing. Toto fell through this trap door in the cyclone; Dorothy caught him by the ear and shut it again.
A little cottage of logs, dusty: nobody has lived here for a year. A bed of dry leaves; on a shelf, an oil-can.
An oil-can on the shelf
Green lemonade and green popcorn
The lemonade seller
You sell green lemonade and green popcorn and green sweets; children pay with green pennies.
A glass of green lemonade? Best in the City!
You pop green popcorn. You are a talker and love gossip about the Palace: they say Oz can take any shape he likes.
Green popcorn, fresh! They say the Great Oz can look like anything he wants, you know.
The green hatter's
You make green hats of every shape, and you are vain about the fashion of the Emerald City.
Every hat in the City is green, and every one of them is mine.
You keep the inn and know travellers from every country of Oz pass through. A Munchkin, a Winkie and a Quadling all stayed last month.
A room for the night? All green, I'm afraid. Everything is, here.
A green marble house
A City merchant's house
A house of green silk curtains
A City family's house
A City grandmother
Welcome! Do take a seat, the green cushions are new.
Business is good, now the roads are safer.
I remember the day the Great Oz came down from the clouds. We built all of this for him.
I work at the Palace, you know. Not that I've seen him.
The emerald jeweller's
You cut and set emeralds; the City is studded with them. You are careful and precise.
Look at the fire in that one. Real emeralds, every stone in the City.
You bake (green-iced) cakes and bread for the City and the Palace.
The Palace ordered sixty green cakes this morning!
The green silk tailor's
You sew green silk clothes; you made the gown laid out for Dorothy in the Palace. Later you help sew the strips of green silk for the Wizard's balloon.
Green silk, of course. What else is there?
